So we have brought as an offering to Hashem such articles of gold as each of us came upon: armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and pendants,cSee note at Exod. 35.22. that expiation may be made for our persons before Hashem.”
Moshe and Elazar the priest accepted the gold from them, all kinds of wrought articles.
All the gold that was offered by the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds as a contribution to Hashem came to 16,750 shekels.—
But in the ranks, everyone kept his booty for himself.—

So Moshe and Elazar the priest accepted the gold from the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds and brought it to the Tent of Meeting, as a reminder in behalf of Bnei Yisrael before Hashem.
The Reuveni and the Gadi owned cattle in very great numbers. Noting that the lands of Yazer and Gilad were a region suitable for cattle,
the Gadi and the Reuveni came to Moshe, Elazar the priest, and the chieftains of the community, and said,
“Atarot, Divon, Yazer, Nimrah, Cheshbon, Elale, Svam, Nevo, and Beon—
the land that Hashem has conquered for the community of Yisrael is cattle country, and your servants have cattle.
It would be a favor to us,” they continued, “if this land were given to your servants as a holding; do not move us across the Yarden.”
Moshe replied to the Gadi and the Reuveni, “Are your brothers to go to war while you stay here?
Why will you turn the minds of Bnei Yisrael from crossing into the land that Hashem has given them?
That is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to survey the land.
After going up to the wadi Eshkol and surveying the land, they turned the minds of Bnei Yisrael from invading the land that Hashem had given them.
Thereupon Hashem was incensed and He swore,
‘None of the men from twenty years up who came out of Mitzrayim shall see the land that I promised on oath to Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov, for they did not remain loyal to Me—
none except Kalev son of Yefuneh the Knizi and Yehoshua son of Nun, for they remained loyal to Hashem.’
Hashem was incensed at Yisrael, and for forty years He made them wander in the wilderness, until the whole generation that had provoked Hashem’s displeasure was gone.
And now you, a breed of sinful men, have replaced your fathers, to add still further to Hashem’s wrath against Yisrael.
If you turn away from Him and He abandons them once more in the wilderness, you will bring calamity upon all this people.”
Then they stepped up to him and said, “We will build here sheepfolds for our flocks and towns for our children.

And we will hastenaMeaning of Heb. hushim uncertain. as shock-troops in the van of Bnei Yisrael until we have established them in their home, while our children stay in the fortified towns because of the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our homes until every one of Bnei Yisrael is in possession of his portion.
But we will not have a share with them in the territory beyond the Yarden, for we have received our share on the east side of the Yarden.”
Moshe said to them, “If you do this, if you go to battle as shock-troops, at the instance of Hashem,
and every shock-fighter among you crosses the Yarden, at the instance of Hashem, until He has dispossessed His enemies before Him,
and the land has been subdued, at the instance of Hashem, and then you return—you shall be clear before Hashem and before Yisrael; and this land shall be your holding under Hashem.
But if you do not do so, you will have sinned against Hashem; and know that your sin will overtake you.
Build towns for your children and sheepfolds for your flocks, but do what you have promised.”
The Gadi and the Reuveni answered Moshe, “Your servants will do as my lord commands.
Our children, our wives, our flocks, and all our other livestock will stay behindbLit. “there.” in the towns of Gilad;
while your servants, all those recruited for war, cross over, at the instance of Hashem, to engage in battle—as my lord orders.”
Then Moshe gave instructions concerning them to Elazar the priest, Yehoshua son of Nun, and the family heads of the Yisraeli tribes.

Moshe said to them, “If every shock-fighter among the Gadi and the Reuveni crosses the Yarden with you to do battle, at the instance of Hashem, and the land is subdued before you, you shall give them the land of Gilad as a holding.
But if they do not cross over with you as shock-troops, they shall receive holdings among you in the land of Kenaan.”
The Gadi and the Reuveni said in reply, “Whatever Hashem has spoken concerning your servants, that we will do.
We ourselves will cross over as shock-troops, at the instance of Hashem, into the land of Kenaan; and we shall keep our hereditary holding across the Yarden.”cI.e., in Transjordan.

So Moshe assigned to them—to the Gadi, the Reuveni, and the half-tribe of Menashe son of Yosef—the kingdom of Sichon king of the Emori and the kingdom of King Og of Bashan, the land with its various cities and the territories of their surrounding towns.
The Gadi rebuilt Divon, Atarot, Aroer,
Atroth-shophan, Yazer, Yogbehah,
Beit Nimrah, and Beit Haran as fortified towns or as enclosures for flocks.
The Reuveni rebuilt Cheshbon, Elale, Kiryatayim,
Nevo, Ba'al Meon—some names being changed—and Sivmah; they gave [their own] names to towns that they rebuilt.dCf. vv. 41, 42.
The descendants of Machir son of Menashe went to Gilad and captured it, dispossessing the Emori who were there;
so Moshe gave Gilad to Machir son of Menashe, and he settled there.
Yair son of Menashe went and captured eOr “the villages of Cham”; cf. Gen. 14.5.their villages,-e which he renamed Chavot Yair.fI.e., “the villages of Yair.”
And Novach went and captured Knat and its dependencies, renaming it Novach after himself.
These were the marches of Bnei Yisrael who started out from the land of Mitzrayim, troop by troop, in the charge of Moshe and Aharon.
Moshe recorded the starting points of their various marches as directed by Hashem. Their marches, by starting points, were as follows:

They set out from Raamses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. It was on the morrow of the passover offering that Bnei Yisrael started out defiantly,aSee note at Exod. 14.8. in plain view of all the Mitzrim.
The Mitzrim meanwhile were burying those among them whom Hashem had struck down, every first-born—whereby Hashem executed judgment on their gods.
Bnei Yisrael set out from Raamses and encamped at Sukkot.
They set out from Sukkot and encamped at Etam, which is on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etam and turned about toward Pi Hachirot, which faces Ba'al Tzfon, and they encamped before Migdol.

They set out from PenebMany Ivri manuscripts and ancient versions read “Pi.”-hahiroth and passed through the sea into the wilderness; and they made a three-days’ journey in the wilderness of Etam and encamped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and came to Eilim. There were twelve springs in Eilim and seventy palm trees, so they encamped there.
They set out from Eilim and encamped by the Sea of Reeds.cSee note at Exod. 10.19.
They set out from the Sea of Reeds and encamped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and encamped at Dofkah.
They set out from Dofkah and encamped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and encamped at Refidim; it was there that the people had no water to drink.
They set out from Refidim and encamped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and encamped at Kivrot Hata'avah.
They set out from Kivrot Hata'avah and encamped at Chatzerot.
They set out from Chatzerot and encamped at Ritmah.
They set out from Ritmah and encamped at Rimon Peretz.
They set out from Rimon Peretz and encamped at Livnah.
They set out from Livnah and encamped at Risah.
They set out from Risah and encamped at Kehelatah.
They set out from Kehelatah and encamped at Mount Shafer.
They set out from Mount Shafer and encamped at Charadah.
They set out from Charadah and encamped at Makhelot.
They set out from Makhelot and encamped at Tachat.
They set out from Tachat and encamped at Terach.
They set out from Terach and encamped at Mitkah.
They set out from Mitkah and encamped at Chashmonah.
They set out from Chashmonah and encamped at Moserot.
They set out from Moserot and encamped at Bnei Ya'akan.
They set out from Bnei Ya'akan and encamped at Chor Hagidgad.
They set out from Chor Hagidgad and encamped at Yotvatah.
They set out from Yotvatah and encamped at Avronah.
They set out from Avronah and encamped at Etzyon Gaver.
They set out from Etzyon Gaver and encamped in the wilderness of Tzin, that is, Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and encamped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
Aharon the priest ascended Mount Hor at the command of Hashem and died there, in the fortieth year after Bnei Yisrael had left the land of Mitzrayim, on the first day of the fifth month.
Aharon was a hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
And the Kenaani, king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negeb, in the land of Kenaan, learned of the coming of Bnei Yisrael.dSee 21.1–3.
They set out from Mount Hor and encamped at Tzalmonah.
They set out from Tzalmonah and encamped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and encamped at Ovot.
They set out from Ovot and encamped at Iyei Ha'avarim, in the territory of Moav.
They set out from Iyim and encamped at Divon Gad.
They set out from Divon Gad and encamped at Almon Divlatayim.
They set out from Almon Divlatayim and encamped in the hills of Avarim, before Nevo.
They set out from the hills of Avarim and encamped in the steppes of Moav, at the Yarden near Yericho;
they encamped by the Yarden from Beit Hayshimot as far as Avel Hashitim, in the steppes of Moav.
In the steppes of Moav, at the Yarden near Yericho, Hashem spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to Bnei Yisrael and say to them: When you cross the Yarden into the land of Kenaan,

you shall dispossess all the inhabitants of the land; you shall destroy all their figuredeSee note at Lev. 26.1. objects; you shall destroy all their molten images, and you shall demolish all their cult places.
And you shall take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have assigned the land to you to possess.

You shall apportion the land among yourselves by lot, clan by clan: with larger groups increase the share, with smaller groups reduce the share. Wherever the lot falls for anyone, that shall be his. You shall have your portions according to your ancestral tribes.

But if you do not dispossess the inhabitants of the land, those whom you allow to remain shall be stings in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and they shall harass you in the land in which you live;
so that I will do to you what I planned to do to them.
Hashem spoke to Moshe, saying:
Instruct Bnei Yisrael and say to them: When you enter the land of Kenaan, this is the land that shall fall to you as your portion, the land of Kenaan with its various boundaries:
Your southern sector shall extend from the wilderness of Tzin alongside Edom. Your southern boundary shall start on the east from the tip of the Dead Sea.
Your boundary shall then turn to pass south of the ascent of Akrabim and continue to Tzin, and its limits shall be south of Kadesh Barnea, reaching Chatzar Adar and continuing to Atzmon.
From Atzmon the boundary shall turn toward the Wadi of Mitzrayim and terminate at the Sea.aI.e., the Mediterranean Sea.
For the western boundary you shall have the coast of the Great Sea;aI.e., the Mediterranean Sea. that shall serve as your western boundary.
This shall be your northern boundary: Draw a line from the Great Sea to Mount Hor;
from Mount Hor draw a line to Levo Chamat,bSee note at 13.21. and let the boundary reach Tzdad.
The boundary shall then run to Zifron and terminate at Chatzar Einan. That shall be your northern boundary.
For your eastern boundary you shall draw a line from Chatzar Einan to Shfam.

From Shfam the boundary shall descend to Rivlah on the east side of Ayin; from there the boundary shall continue downward and abut on the eastern slopes of the Sea of Kineret.cI.e., the Sea (or Lake) of Galil.

The boundary shall then descend along the Yarden and terminate at the Dead Sea.
That shall be your land as defined by its boundaries on all sides.
Moshe instructed Bnei Yisrael, saying: This is the land you are to receive by lot as your hereditary portion, which Hashem has commanded to be given to the nine and a half tribes.
For the Ruveni tribe by its ancestral houses, the Gadi tribe by its ancestral houses, and the half-tribe of Menashe have already received their portions:
those two and a half tribes have received their portions across the Yarden, opposite Yericho, on the east, the orient side.
Hashem spoke to Moshe, saying:
These are the names of the men through whom the land shall be apportioned for you: Elazar the priest and Yehoshua son of Nun.
And you shall also take a chieftain from each tribe through whom the land shall be apportioned.
These are the names of the men: from the tribe of Yehudah: Kalev son of Yefuneh.
From the Shimoni tribe: ShmueldOr “Shmuel.” son of Amihud.
From the tribe of Binyamin: Elidad son of Kislon.
From the Dani tribe: a chieftain, Buki son of Yogli.
For the descendants of Yosef: from the Menashi tribe: a chieftain, Chaniel son of Ephod;
and from the Efrati tribe: a chieftain, Kmuel son of Shiftan.
From the Zevuloni tribe: a chieftain, Elitzafan son of Parnach.
From the Issacharite tribe: a chieftain, Paltiel son of Azan.
From the Asherite tribe: a chieftain, Achihud son of Shlomi.
From the Naphtalite tribe: a chieftain, Pedahel son of Amihud.
It was these whom Hashem designated to allot portions to Bnei Yisrael in the land of Kenaan.
Hashem spoke to Moshe in the steppes of Moav at the Yarden near Yericho, saying:
Instruct Bnei Yisrael to assign, out of the holdings apportioned to them, towns for the Leviyim to dwell in; you shall also assign to the Leviyim pasture land around their towns.
The towns shall be theirs to dwell in, and the pasture shall be for the cattle they own and all their other beasts.
The town pasture that you are to assign to the Leviyim shall extend a thousand cubits outside the town wall all around.

You shall measure off two thousand cubits outside the town on the east side, two thousand on the south side, two thousand on the west side, and two thousand on the north side, with the town in the center. That shall be the pasture for their towns.
The towns that you assign to the Leviyim shall comprise the six cities of refuge that you are to designate for a manslayer to flee to, to which you shall add forty-two towns.
Thus the total of the towns that you assign to the Leviyim shall be forty-eight towns, with their pasture.
In assigning towns from the holdings of Bnei Yisrael, take more from the larger groups and less from the smaller, so that each assigns towns to the Leviyim in proportion to the share it receives.
Hashem spoke further to Moshe:
Speak to Bnei Yisrael and say to them: When you cross the Yarden into the land of Kenaan,
you shall provide yourselves with places to serve you as cities of refuge to which a manslayer who has killed a person unintentionally may flee.
The cities shall serve you as a refuge from the avenger,aLit. “redeemer,” i.e., next of kin; cf. note at Lev. 25.25. so that the manslayer may not die unless he has stood trial before the assembly.
The towns that you thus assign shall be six cities of refuge in all.
Three cities shall be designated beyond the Yarden, and the other three shall be designated in the land of Kenaan: they shall serve as cities of refuge.
These six cities shall serve Bnei Yisrael and the resident aliens among them for refuge, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
Anyone, however, who strikes another with an iron object so that death results is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
If he struck him with a stone toolbLit. “of the hand.” that could cause death, and death resulted, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
Similarly, if the object with which he struck him was a wooden toolbLit. “of the hand.” that could cause death, and death resulted, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
The blood-avenger himself shall put the murderer to death; it is he who shall put him to death upon encounter.
So, too, if he pushed him in hate or hurled something at him on purpose and death resulted,
or if he struck him with his hand in enmity and death resulted, the assailant shall be put to death; he is a murderer. The blood-avenger shall put the murderer to death upon encounter.
But if he pushed him without malice aforethought or hurled any object at him unintentionally,
or inadvertentlycLit. “without seeing.” dropped upon him any deadly object of stone, and death resulted—though he was not an enemy of his and did not seek his harm—
in such cases the assembly shall decide between the slayer and the blood-avenger.

The assembly shall protect the manslayer from the blood-avenger, and the assembly shall restore him to the city of refuge to which he fled, and there he shall remain until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the sacred oil.
But if the manslayer ever goes outside the limits of the city of refuge to which he has fled,
and the blood-avenger comes upon him outside the limits of his city of refuge, and the blood-avenger kills the manslayer, there is no bloodguilt on his account.
For he must remain inside his city of refuge until the death of the high priest; after the death of the high priest, the manslayer may return to his land holding.
Such shall be your law of procedure throughout the ages in all your settlements.
If anyone kills a person, the manslayer may be executed only on the evidence of witnesses; the testimony of a single witness against a person shall not suffice for a sentence of death.
You may not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of a capital crime; he must be put to death.
Nor may you accept ransom in lieu of flight to a city of refuge, enabling one to return to live on his land before the death of the priest.
You shall not pollute the land in which you live; for blood pollutes the land, and the land can have no expiation for blood that is shed on it, except by the blood of him who shed it.
You shall not defile the land in which you live, in which I Myself abide, for I Hashem abide among Bnei Yisrael.

The family heads in the clan of the descendants of Gilad son of Machir son of Menashe, one of the Josephite clans, came forward and appealed to Moshe and the chieftains, family headsaI.e., tribal heads. of Bnei Yisrael.
They said, “Hashem commanded my lord to assign the land to Bnei Yisrael as shares by lot, and my lord was further commanded by Hashem to assign the share of our kinsman Tzelofchad to his daughters.

Now, if they marry persons from another Yisraeli tribe, their share will be cut off from our ancestral portion and be added to the portion of the tribe into which they marry; thus our allotted portion will be diminished.
And even when Bnei Yisrael observe the jubilee, their share will be added to that of the tribe into which they marry, and their share will be cut off from the ancestral portion of our tribe.”
So Moshe, at Hashem’s bidding, instructed Bnei Yisrael, saying: “The plea of the Josephite tribe is just.
This is what Hashem has commanded concerning the daughters of Tzelofchad: They may marry anyone they wish, provided they marry into a clan of their father’s tribe.
No inheritance of Bnei Yisrael may pass over from one tribe to another, but Bnei Yisrael must remain bound each to the ancestral portion of his tribe.
Every daughter among the Yisraeli tribes who inherits a share must marry someone from a clan of her father’s tribe, in order that every Yisraeli may keep his ancestral share.
Thus no inheritance shall pass over from one tribe to another, but the Yisraeli tribes shall remain bound each to its portion.”
The daughters of Tzelofchad did as Hashem had commanded Moshe:
Machlah, Tirtzah, Choglah, Milkah, and No'ah, Tzelofchad’s daughters, were married to sons of their uncles,
marrying into clans of descendants of Menashe son of Yosef; and so their share remained in the tribe of their father’s clan.
These are the commandments and regulations that Hashem enjoined upon Bnei Yisrael, through Moshe, on the steppes of Moav, at the Yarden near Yericho.
